data.title: Polymarket and Yahoo Finance end prediction market pact
data.description:
Yahoo Finance ended a partnership with Polymarket (POLYMARKET) that allowed it to use Polymarket data for a prediction market hub on its website, according to a media report on Friday.

The companies forged the agreement last November. At the time, Polymarket said its probability data for key economic, government, and market outcomes would be paired with related news, quotes, and analysis from Yahoo Finance and its partners. "By combining trusted data with in-depth analysis, the hub will empower investors to make smarter, more strategic prediction market investments," Polymarket said  in a social media post.

The predictions market hub was removed in April, and the partnership agreement ended, Bloomberg News reported.  A spokesperson told Bloomberg, "That specific agreement ended, but Polymarket continues to be an advertising partner across Yahoo, and we’re open to similar types of partnerships."

Polymarket (POLYMARKET) and its rival, Kalshi (KALSHI), have entered agreements with a number of news websites, broadcasters, and publications. For example, Polymarket entered an agreement with News Corp.'s (NWSA) Dow Jones division, which publishes the Wall Street Journal and Barron's. Kalshi has inked partnerships with Warner Bros. Discovery's (WBD) CNN, Versant Media Group's (VSNT) CNBC, and Fox Corp. (FOX).

data.title: Trump set to announce MFN pricing for Medicaid in all states
data.description:
• President Trump on Friday will announce that Medicaid beneficiaries in all 50 states will benefit from "Most Favored Nation" pricing discounts for some prescription drugs.
  • While Medicaid programs already receive significant discounts from pharmaceutical companies, the White House Council of Economic Advisers projects the move will lead to $27.6B in savings for state governments and $36.6B for the federal government over 10 years, according to Semafor, which broke the news. 
  • The news website noted that Trump will have a meeting today with the governors of Arkansas, Mississippi, and South Dakota to discuss progress on lowering drug prices.
  • An AARP Public Policy Institute report released in August found that if MFN pricing were implemented for the top 10 drugs spent on Medicare Part D and Part B in 2025, Medicare spending on them would drop from $273B to $76B between 2029 and 2033.

data.title: S&P 500 over-earning is a temporary bump, not a bubble - Goldman
Morgan Stanley sees managed competition ahead of Trump-Xi summit
data.description:
The U.S.-China relationship is likely to remain in a phase of "managed competition" as President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping prepare to meet next week, with Morgan Stanley expecting the summit to focus on extending the existing trade and rare-earth truce rather than delivering a broader reset.

The Sept. 24 Washington meeting is likely to build on commitments from the May summit, with fewer new deliverables outside traditional trade measures and an extension of the rare-earth truce, Morgan Stanley said.

Trade truce remains the focal point

Morgan Stanley said the summit would be a test of whether the existing trade truce can withstand targeted escalation and extend beyond its Nov. 10 expiry. The firm said the two sides remain mutually dependent in areas including rare earths and chip exports while gradually building more distinct technology ecosystems.

Three measures are due to expire on Nov. 10: the suspension of the BIS Affiliates Rule, China's pause on its second-wave rare-earth controls, and 178 U.S. Section 301 tariff exclusions. Morgan Stanley expects both sides to prioritize extending those measures, potentially with modifications.

On tariffs, the firm expects some targeted rollback while the broader tariff framework remains intact. U.S. and Chinese teams are negotiating a framework covering roughly $30B of nonsensitive trade on each side, which Morgan Stanley said would be economically modest relative to total bilateral trade but could provide tangible progress without touching strategically sensitive areas.

The Trump administration is likely to delay announcing new tariffs on China and other countries related to alleged excess manufacturing capacity until after the Trump-Xi summit, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. 

The administration had previously planned to release a trade report ahead of the meeting recommending a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods, according to the background provided.

The timing of the tariff announcement and the eventual rate remain uncertain. Morgan Stanley said potential Section 301 overcapacity tariffs could remain an “overhang” even beyond the summit.

AI rivalry follows a separate path

While trade negotiations remain focused on preserving the existing framework, Morgan Stanley said competition over artificial intelligence is increasingly developing on a separate track.

The firm expects the U.S. to seek cooperation with China on monitoring AI-directed cyberattacks and discussions around AI regulation while pursuing a "middle path" on restrictions that would leave below-frontier AI capabilities relatively intact while controlling frontier technologies. China, meanwhile, is seeking greater visibility into how Washington will regulate future frontier models, Morgan Stanley said.

Morgan Stanley said the broader technology rivalry is likely to continue even if the trade truce is extended, with both countries pursuing greater supply-chain independence in areas including critical minerals, semiconductors, and AI infrastructure.

Market impact considered limited

Morgan Stanley said expectations for the summit are low, which could limit the market reaction to an extension of the trade truce. The firm said macro weakness, regulatory concerns, and liquidity headwinds remain more important near-term constraints for Chinese equities.

The firm also said the broader relationship would continue to be defined by sector-specific competition within a framework of managed competition. Its assessment was that the Washington summit would represent an effort to reinforce that framework rather than resolve the core disputes over advanced technology and critical minerals.

Morgan Stanley said the two countries' efforts to reduce strategic supply-chain dependencies would continue even under managed competition, supporting themes around economic security, reindustrialization, and AI sovereignty.

data.title: Meta's personal AI agent Muse hits No. 1 on Apple's App Store
data.description:
Meta Platforms' (META) Muse app, a personal AI agent that goes beyond a chatbot and executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf, has reached the No. 1 spot on Apple's (AAPL) U.S. App Store a little over one week after its release.

The app quickly rose above its competitors, as OpenAI's (OPENAI) ChatGPT sits at No. 2, Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) Gemini is No. 8 and Anthropic's (ANTHRO) Claude comes in at No. 13. Way down the list, SpaceXAI's (SPCX) Grok lands at No. 32 and Microsoft (MSFT) Copilot ranks No. 64.

"Anyone can use it out of the box, no technical experience required," according to Meta. "It can handle tasks, like sending an email or booking travel, and it can take on big audacious goals. Once a person shares a goal with Muse, it helps them develop a personalized plan and coordinate their time and resources, then advances the work on its own. It can open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate on their behalf."

Muse can also keep working in the background even when a user has closed the app and can check in for approval before completing certain tasks.

"A week after launch, Muse is now the #1 app in the App Store!" said Meta Chief AI Officer Alexander Wang in a post on X on Friday. "It's been SO exciting to see how much y'all have done with Muse. We can't wait to do more together!"

data.title: Global ex-US equities retain bullish outlook despite tighter policy
data.description:
Global ex-US equities retain a bullish backdrop despite rising valuation and monetary-policy risks, according to Callum Thomas, Head of Research and Founder of Topdown Charts, who said the latest Federal Reserve rate hike reinforces a shift toward tighter global policy.

Thomas said his assessment of global ex-US, or rest-of-world, equities remains bullish in absolute terms, while the relative case against U.S. stocks is also showing signs of improvement.

Technical indicators remain supportive, with equities in an uptrend and breadth remaining strong. However, policy conditions that have provided a tailwind are beginning to turn less supportive, while valuations, although still reasonable and significantly cheaper than in the U.S., have already risen substantially.

Thomas noted that the bullish case is less compelling than it was in 2024 and 2025, when valuations were lower and monetary policy was moving toward rate cuts. The Federal Reserve's latest 25-basis-point rate hike to 4% adds to what Thomas described as a broader global shift toward rate increases.

He also pointed to the relatively high valuation starting point for U.S. equities, which could leave them exposed if the policy and inflation backdrop becomes less favorable.

On relative performance, Thomas said global equities are still in the process of turning around a roughly 15-year period of U.S. outperformance. Emerging markets have driven much of the improvement so far, while developed markets outside the U.S. have also shown signs of strength.

However, he said the macro and fundamental catalysts needed for a sustained shift remain inconsistent, with relative earnings performance still favoring the U.S. and the dollar continuing to hold support after a brief decline from its peak. A sustained period of dollar weakness and stronger earnings growth outside the U.S. would provide additional confirmation, he said.

Earnings are meanwhile emerging as a key support for the global ex-US outlook, Thomas said. All three major segments of global equities are seeing upgrades to long-term earnings-growth expectations alongside improving forward EPS trends.

Emerging markets, particularly Korea and Taiwan, are an important driver, while developed markets outside the U.S. are also seeing earnings growth accelerate.

Thomas said the combination of improving earnings, tentative gains in relative price performance and still-cheaper valuations supports the bullish absolute outlook, although the significant valuation re-rating and global shift toward tighter monetary policy mean risks have become less favorable than in previous years.

data.title: Volkswagen recalls more than 208,000 US vehicles over steering defect
data.description:
Volkswagen (VWAGY) is recalling more than 208,000 vehicles in the US after a steering-rack mounting bolt was found to be vulnerable to corrosion and breakage, potentially resulting in a loss of steering control.

The recall covers 208,724 vehicles, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The affected models include certain 2018 Tiguan SUVs, 2018 and 2019 Atlas vehicles, and 2019 through 2021 Audi Q3 models.

The right-side steering-rack mounting bolt can corrode over time and fracture, the US auto-safety regulator said. A failure could lead to a loss of steering control and increase the risk of a crash.

As part of the recall, dealers will replace the affected steering-rack mounting bolt at no cost to vehicle owners, according to NHTSA.

Shares were trading about 7% lower on Friday.
